issue.title: [Bug] Kimi Code 新 K3.1 型号缺少思考能力声明，经 Magpie 接入报 400 disabled thinking mode
issue.body:
## 问题

官方 Magpie 0.1.1349 接入 Kimi Code 1.1.2 后，新型号 `k3.1-pro` / `k3.1-pro-highspeed` 被本机模型目录标成不支持思考，生成的 Kimi 模型配置也缺少思考能力声明。Kimi 会话因此以 `thinkingEffort: "off"` 运行，Kimi Code 上游拒绝请求：

```text
400 Kimi Code: K3.1 Pro does not support disabled thinking mode.
Please enable thinking and try again, or choose another model.
provider.api_error · HTTP 400
```

Mac 上使用 **Kimi 自带的 K3.1 Pro** 正常；这是原生入口对照，不是“同一条 Magpie 路由在 Mac 上已验证正常”。

## 环境及已观察到的证据

- 出错端：Windows x64，官方 Magpie **0.1.1349**，Kimi Code 桌面版 **1.1.2**。
- 路由：Magpie 内置 Kimi Code 供应商，模型完整 ID 为 `kimi/k3.1-pro`，Kimi 配置别名为 `magpie/kimi/k3.1-pro`。
- Kimi 全局配置已经是 `[thinking] enabled = true`。
- 真实 Kimi 会话的 wire 记录在报错前多次保存 `model: "kimi/k3.1-pro"`、`modelAlias: "magpie/kimi/k3.1-pro"`、`thinkingEffort: "off"`。
- 真实 Magpie 用量记录显示这条路由连续返回 HTTP 400。
- 两个 K3.1 型号在本机 Magpie `/v1/models` 中均为：

```json
{
  "reasoning": false,
  "reasoning_levels": [],
  "supported_reasoning_levels": []
}
```

生成配置与 Kimi 自带模型配置的能力对照（仅展示不含凭据的字段）：

```toml
[models."magpie/kimi/k3.1-pro"]
provider = "magpie"
model = "kimi/k3.1-pro"
capabilities = ["image_in", "tool_use"]

[models."kimi-code/k3.1-pro"]
provider = "managed:kimi-code"
model = "k3.1-pro"
capabilities = [
  "thinking", "always_thinking", "image_in",
  "video_in", "tool_use", "dynamically_loaded_tools"
]
```

高速版的思考声明也有相同差异。额外的图片/视频/动态工具能力差异不是本报告所主张的 400 根因。

## 定位

v0.1.1349 对应源码提交为 `7cafa26c499ec800412d2c843dd9107ebf4c8a67`。在 [kimiModelTables](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/7cafa26c499ec800412d2c843dd9107ebf4c8a67/internal/agent/kimi.go#L96) 中，只有 `len(m.Efforts) > 0` 才向 Kimi 写入 `thinking`；当前这两个新型号的目录没有思考档位，因此该能力被遗漏。该生成代码也没有为不可关闭思考的模型写入 `always_thinking`。

读取已安装 Kimi Code 1.1.2 中未修改的纯能力判断函数，并以实际配置执行时，原生两个型号均识别为支持思考、默认 Max；Magpie 生成的两个型号均识别为不支持思考、默认 Off。此检查没有启动模型请求，也没有修改客户端文件。

报告时检查的最新主分支为 `84341795`；相关 Kimi 配置生成位置尚未发现 `k3.1` 或 `always_thinking` 的适配。

## 自定义提示词插件的排查边界

出错端同时启用了 KupaDesk 0.0.15。为了区分插件改参和接入兼容性问题，额外做了独立对照：

- 对当前安装插件及两个真实模型绑定做了 **24 项本地检查**：提示词可以加入，原请求的思考参数、工具声明、工具结果及历史保持不变，重试不重复注入。检查结果不代表模型一定遵循提示词。
- 使用 **未修改的官方 Magpie 0.1.1349**、临时 HOME、虚拟凭据和回环模拟上游，完成 **48 组对照**：插件关闭、异步 Hook、同步 middleware fallback × 两个型号 × 四种思考档位 × 流式/非流式。
- 插件开关之间，上游收到的思考参数、工具和非指令历史一致。模拟上游对关闭思考返回相同 400，其他档位返回 200。
- 这 48 组是验证插件是否改参的**本地模拟测试**，没有调用真实 Kimi 模型，不能当作真实供应商端到端成功测试。

这些结果支持优先修复 Magpie 的模型能力/配置生成层，而不是在提示词中补救或让提示词插件强改思考参数。

## 期望

1. 能从可靠目录或 Kimi Code 的型号能力元数据正确识别新 K3.1 型号的思考能力和档位。
2. 在生成 Kimi 模型配置时声明思考能力；供应商明确为 thinking-only 的型号同时声明不可关闭思考的能力。
3. 模型能力未知时不要默默把这类已知要求思考的型号呈现为无思考模型。
4. 保留原登录、用户显式配置和其他模型行为，不通过修改官方客户端文件来解决。

本次仅排查和反馈，未修改现用官方程序、插件、配置、提示词或模型绑定；没有附带私人提示词、会话正文、登录信息、密钥或原始日志。

comments.body: Taking this. Root-cause direction verified on current main (dd1e8822): internal/agent/kimi.go:97 only writes the `thinking` capability when `len(m.Efforts) > 0`, and neither `k3.1-pro` nor `k3.1-pro-highspeed` carries thinking efforts in the Kimi model tables (no `k3.1` adaptation on main), so the generated Kimi config omits thinking and the session runs with `thinkingEffort: "off"`, which K3.1 rejects with 400. Will follow with a fix on my fork.

Kimi Code's new K3.1 models get `always_thinking` in the tables magpie writes, so Off is no longer offered on them and the 400 is unreachable through the picker.

What you hit has two layers. The first is the catalog: models.dev, where magpie's model levels come from, did not list the two new models yet, so `/v1/models` showed `reasoning: false` with empty level lists, and `internal/agent/kimi.go` (`len(m.Efforts) > 0`) wrote no `thinking` capability — the session ran at `thinkingEffort: "off"` and the upstream refused it. That half heals itself: models.dev (fetched today, 2026-10-24) now lists `k3.1-pro` and `k3.1-pro-highspeed` under both `kimi-code-plan` catalogs with effort `low, high, max` and no off — matching your Kimi-side reading (thinking on, default Max) — and magpie refreshes that catalog at most a day stale on its own.

The second layer is code, and it is what this patch fixes: even with the levels known, magpie's generated tables said `thinking` alone. Kimi's own entries for these models declare a second capability, `always_thinking` — thinking cannot be turned off — and without it Kimi Code still offers Off beside the levels, so the refused state stays one click away. Magpie now writes `always_thinking` beside `thinking` for exactly the models whose levels have no off among them (the same rule WorkBuddy's `canDisableThinking` follows), and leaves kimi-cli out of it, as with `tool_use`: the old CLI refuses words it doesn't know. A model that has an off level (`k3`, `kimi-for-coding`) is written as before.

After this patch and a catalog refresh, magpie's table for `k3.1-pro` reads `capabilities = ["thinking", "always_thinking", "tool_use"]`, `support_efforts = ["low", "high", "max"]`, `default_effort = "high"`; `k3` stays `["thinking", "tool_use"]` with its off level. The image/video/`dynamically_loaded_tools` differences you measured are left alone — you're right that they are not what returns the 400.

## What changed

- `internal/agent/kimi.go`, `kimiModelTables`: when a model has reasoning levels and none of them is `none`, the new Kimi Code's table also gets `"always_thinking"` in `capabilities`, beside `"thinking"` (kimi-cli's tables are not told, `!legacy`, as for `tool_use`). Nothing else about the capabilities, `support_efforts` or `default_effort` changes.
- `internal/agent/kimi_efforts_test.go`: new `TestKimiAlwaysThinking` (a no-none model's table declares `thinking`, `always_thinking` and the levels; a has-none model's doesn't get the word; kimi-cli's table gets neither new word), and the `wide` row of `TestKimiEfforts` (levels `low, medium`, no off) now expects the word too.

## Verification

(darwin/arm64, go 1.26.8, tests under a temp `HOME`)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| after, `go test -tags nogui -run 'TestKimiAlwaysThinking|TestKimiEfforts' ./internal/agent/` | ok |
| before (baseline `dd1e8822`), same command | FAIL: k3.1-pro row `{Capabilities:[thinking tool_use] …}`, want `[thinking always_thinking tool_use]` |
| ablation: only `internal/agent/kimi.go` reverted to `dd1e8822`, tests kept | FAIL: `TestKimiAlwaysThinking` (k3.1-pro row) and `TestKimiEfforts` (`wide` row); restored from the commit, green again |
| `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./internal/agent/` (full package) | ok but `TestMothX`, which fails the same on a clean `dd1e8822` worktree (pre-existing on this machine: a `mothx` on its `PATH`); no other red |
| `gofmt -l` on the two touched files | clean |
| `go vet ./...` | OK |
| `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...` | OK |
| `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` | OK |
| `go build -tags nogui .` (darwin), `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui .`, `GOOS=windows go build .` | OK |
| models.dev fetched 2026-10-24 | both `kimi-code-plan-cn` and `-global` list `k3.1-pro` / `k3.1-pro-highspeed`, `reasoning_options` = effort `["low","high","max"]`, no toggle |

## Not verified

- Not exercised against a real Kimi Code 1.1.2 install or the live upstream: the capability names and levels written are the ones you measured in Kimi's own entries for these models, and the schema is the one Kimi itself writes; a session against the real vendor is the one thing this sandbox cannot do.
- The catalog half (the models' levels) rides in with models.dev and magpie's own refresh; verified by fetching models.dev today, not from this repo's fixture, whose snapshot (2026-10-09) predates the models.
- `default_effort` stays `high` (magpie's rule for every model, #333) rather than Kimi's Max default — any level it starts on is an enabled one, so this does not reintroduce the 400.
**Attribution**: AI-written; I've read the whole diff and the tests pass. Please keep the author (`ggbdpq`) or add `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>`.

Branch with the commit: [hunt74-b-kimi-k31-thinking](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt74-b-kimi-k31-thinking) (head `03b9f53e705da9dc19566c25c403a17205a8dd79`).

已在我的 fork 分支 `fix/3399-kimi-thinking` 修好（head `d19b48b8`，基于 upstream `6afbe3f3`）：Kimi 的思考型模型即使没有 off 档也声明出能力。

**根因**：`internal/agent/kimi.go` 的 capabilities 只在 `len(m.Efforts) > 0` 时追加 `"thinking"`。一个能思考、但目录里的档位没有 off 的模型因此什么能力都没写，会话按 `thinkingEffort:"off"` 跑，K3.1 直接 400 `disabled thinking mode`。

**改动**：能思考但没有 off 档的模型补上 `always_thinking`（键名取自报告者贴出的 Kimi Code 1.1.2 原生模型表；仓库里没有这个键的既有证据，所以只有这条路径写它）；有 off 档的模型保持原来只写 `thinking`；kimi-cli（legacy）两个新键都不写。

**验证**：红 —— `go test -tags nogui ./internal/agent/ -run TestKimiEfforts` → `magpie/think/toggled: {Capabilities:[tool_use] …} want [thinking always_thinking tool_use]`；绿 —— `同一命令与 `./internal/agent` 全包（18s）通过；Kimi 其余接线测试不受影响` → `ok github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/agent`。

没有真 Kimi K3.1 账号做端到端验证；键名来源已在上面说明，若与你手上的原生表不一致请指出。

补充：本轮所有分支合起来的 `go test -tags nogui ./...` 是 70 个包 ok、5 个包红（edit `TestWriteAtomicReadOnlyHardLink`、gateway 五个、plugin `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`、provider `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials` 的 synctest fatal、testenv `TestProgram`），这五个在基线 `6afbe3f3`、本机 umask 0027 下逐字同样红，不是这次改动带来的。

分支：https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/3399-kimi-thinking。没有开 PR（本仓库不收外部 PR）；如果更希望直接把 patch 贴在这里，说一声即可。

Checked main first (`e056779a`, today): neither fix has landed — `kimiModelTables` there still writes `thinking` only for models with levels, and `always_thinking` appears nowhere under `internal/agent/`.

@skygunner your branch is the same fix in the same spot as the patch attached to our Oct 24 comment above ([branch `hunt74-b-kimi-k31-thinking`](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt74-b-kimi-k31-thinking), head `03b9f53e`, based on `dd1e8822`; yours head `d19b48b8`, based on `6afbe3f3`) — good to see the root cause independently corroborated. A mechanical comparison, for whoever picks:

**Same in both:**

- The write itself is identical line for line: a model with levels, none of them `none`, gets `always_thinking` beside `thinking` in the new Kimi Code's table; a model whose levels include `none` keeps `thinking` alone; kimi-cli is told neither word (`!legacy`), as with `tool_use`.
- Both extend the `wide` row of `TestKimiEfforts` the same way (`thinking, always_thinking, tool_use`).

**Different:**

- The gate on the `thinking` word itself: ours leaves it at `len(m.Efforts) > 0`; yours widens it to `m.Reasoning || len(m.Efforts) > 0`, which adds a face ours doesn't cover — a model the catalog marks as thinking but names no levels for gets `thinking, always_thinking` in yours, no capability word in ours. Whether an unknown-levels model should be declared always-thinking is a real call for the maintainer: levels unknown may also mean levels wrong.
- Tests: ours adds a separate `TestKimiAlwaysThinking` (a levels-known pair plus the legacy table); yours adds a `toggled` row to `TestKimiEfforts` for the Reasoning-no-levels face. Different faces; they would combine cleanly.

Both branches stay up as they are — ours isn't withdrawn. The shared core is one line and either patch carries it; maintainer's pick.

Not tried against the real Kimi upstream; the e2e ran Kimi Code 2.4.1 against a fake upstream serving the real list.

That half heals itself: models.dev (fetched today, 2026-10-24) now lists `k3.1-pro` and `k3.1-pro-highspeed` under both `kimi-code-plan` catalogs with effort `low, high, max` and no off — matching your Kimi-side reading (thinking on, default Max) — and magpie refreshes that catalog at most a day stale on its own.

The second layer is code, and it is what this patch fixes: even with the levels known, magpie's generated tables said `thinking` alone. Kimi's own entries for these models declare a second capability, `always_thinking` — thinking cannot be turned off — and without it Kimi Code still offers Off beside the levels, so the refused state stays one click away. Magpie now writes `always_thinking` beside `thinking` for exactly the models whose levels have no off among them (the same rule WorkBuddy's `canDisableThinking` follows), and leaves kimi-cli out of it, as with `tool_use`: the old CLI refuses words it doesn't know. A model that has an off level (`k3`, `kimi-for-coding`) is written as before.

After this patch and a catalog refresh, magpie's table for `k3.1-pro` reads `capabilities = ["thinking", "always_thinking", "tool_use"]`, `support_efforts = ["low", "high", "max"]`, `default_effort = "high"`; `k3` stays `["thinking", "tool_use"]` with its off level. The image/video/`dynamically_loaded_tools` differences you measured are left alone — you're right that they are not what returns the 400.

## What changed

- `internal/agent/kimi.go`, `kimiModelTables`: when a model has reasoning levels and none of them is `none`, the new Kimi Code's table also gets `"always_thinking"` in `capabilities`, beside `"thinking"` (kimi-cli's tables are not told, `!legacy`, as for `tool_use`). Nothing else about the capabilities, `support_efforts` or `default_effort` changes.
- `internal/agent/kimi_efforts_test.go`: new `TestKimiAlwaysThinking` (a no-none model's table declares `thinking`, `always_thinking` and the levels; a has-none model's doesn't get the word; kimi-cli's table gets neither new word), and the `wide` row of `TestKimiEfforts` (levels `low, medium`, no off) now expects the word too.

issue.title: ZCode takeover writes variants/defaultVariant into the reasoning config — ZCode 3.12.3 reads levels/defaultLevel/providerOptionsByLevel, so it never sends `thinking`

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## What happens

When magpie takes over the ZCode agent, every request ZCode sends through the magpie gateway carries only `output_config: {"effort": …}` and **no Anthropic `thinking` field**. For always-thinking upstream models (e.g. the Kimi Code membership `kimi/k3.1-pro`) every turn 400s:

```text
Kimi Code: K3.1 Pro does not support disabled thinking mode.
Please enable thinking and try again, or choose another model.
```

This is the same symptom as #3739 (gateway retry wording) and #3399 (Kimi Code agent catalog), but the root cause on the ZCode side is different and not covered there: **the model config magpie writes into ZCode uses keys ZCode does not read, so ZCode never learns it should emit `thinking`.**

## Evidence

ZCode 3.12.3 model-reasoning schema (from `resources/glm/zcode.cjs`):

```js
MSs = { enabled?: boolean, levels?: string[], defaultLevel?: string,
        providerOptionsByLevel?: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>> }
// model config: { ..., reasoning?: boolean | MSs, ... }.passthrough()
```

What magpie 0.1.1687 writes into `~/.zcode/v2/config.json` (and mirrors into `~/.zcode/v2/provider_config.json` → `providerModelRules`):

```json
"reasoning": { "enabled": true, "variants": ["low","high","max"], "defaultVariant": "high" }
```

`variants`/`defaultVariant` are not in the schema; passthrough keeps them but they are ignored. With no `levels` and no `providerOptionsByLevel`, the effort selector still appears and `output_config.effort` is sent, but nothing ever maps a level to `thinking: {"type":"enabled"}`.

Confirmed by three observations on Linux x64, magpie 0.1.1687, ZCode 3.12.3, Kimi Code membership provider (`kimi` preset):

1. ZCode model-io logs: requests to `kimi/k3.1-pro` have `output_config.effort = "max"`, no `thinking` key — while native GLM requests from the same build do carry `thinking: {"type":"enabled"}`.
2. Gateway A/B (direct curl to `http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/messages`, model `kimi/k3.1-pro`): with `thinking: {"type":"enabled"}` → 200; without it → the 400 above.
3. Adding the schema-correct keys fixes it: per-model `map` expressions (in `optionSpecs.reasoningLevel`) of the form `reasoningLevel == "disabled" ? {thinking:{type:"disabled"}} : {thinking:{type:"enabled"}, output_config:{effort: reasoningLevel}}` make ZCode send `thinking`, and the model works.

## A second, related problem: magpie clobbers user fixes in `providerModelRules`

Switching the ZCode agent model in magpie (e.g. `magpie zcode <model>` to another model and back) rewrites `~/.zcode/v2/provider_config.json` and wipes any user-added `map` inside `providerModelRules`. ZCode loads `[...providerModelRules, ...manualProviderModelRules]` and resolves exact matches from the end, so overrides placed in `manualProviderModelRules` survive magpie rewrites — that is where we had to put the fix. Fixing this in magpie itself (writing the keys ZCode reads) would remove the need for any local patch.

## Suggested fix

When generating ZCode provider/model config, emit the schema ZCode reads, e.g.:

```json
"reasoning": {
  "enabled": true,
  "levels": ["low","high","max"],
  "defaultLevel": "high",
  "providerOptionsByLevel": {
    "low":  {"thinking": {"type": "enabled"}},
    "high": {"thinking": {"type": "enabled"}},
    "max":  {"thinking": {"type": "enabled"}}
  }
}
```

(or the equivalent `map` expression form in `provider_config.json`), with `thinking: {"type":"disabled"}` for levels named `disabled`/`none` when the model offers them.

## Environment

- Linux x64, magpie **0.1.1687** (also reproduced the takeover config shape on 0.1.1589)
- ZCode **3.12.3** (Electron; schema read from its bundled `resources/glm/zcode.cjs`)
- Provider: built-in Kimi Code membership preset (`kimi`), endpoint `https://api.kimi.com/coding`
- Client path: ZCode → magpie gateway `http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/messages` (anthropic)

Happy to provide full request/response captures if useful — and thanks for magpie, it works beautifully otherwise.

timeline.body:
Checked main first (`e056779a`, today): neither fix has landed — `kimiModelTables` there still writes `thinking` only for models with levels, and `always_thinking` appears nowhere under `internal/agent/`.

@skygunner your branch is the same fix in the same spot as the patch attached to our Oct 24 comment above ([branch `hunt74-b-kimi-k31-thinking`](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/hunt74-b-kimi-k31-thinking), head `03b9f53e`, based on `dd1e8822`; yours head `d19b48b8`, based on `6afbe3f3`) — good to see the root cause independently corroborated. A mechanical comparison, for whoever picks:

**Same in both:**

- The write itself is identical line for line: a model with levels, none of them `none`, gets `always_thinking` beside `thinking` in the new Kimi Code's table; a model whose levels include `none` keeps `thinking` alone; kimi-cli is told neither word (`!legacy`), as with `tool_use`.
- Both extend the `wide` row of `TestKimiEfforts` the same way (`thinking, always_thinking, tool_use`).

**Different:**

- The gate on the `thinking` word itself: ours leaves it at `len(m.Efforts) > 0`; yours widens it to `m.Reasoning || len(m.Efforts) > 0`, which adds a face ours doesn't cover — a model the catalog marks as thinking but names no levels for gets `thinking, always_thinking` in yours, no capability word in ours. Whether an unknown-levels model should be declared always-thinking is a real call for the maintainer: levels unknown may also mean levels wrong.
- Tests: ours adds a separate `TestKimiAlwaysThinking` (a levels-known pair plus the legacy table); yours adds a `toggled` row to `TestKimiEfforts` for the Reasoning-no-levels face. Different faces; they would combine cleanly.

Both branches stay up as they are — ours isn't withdrawn. The shared core is one line and either patch carries it; maintainer's pick.

2ac423f4f (v0.1.2267) covers this: a Kimi Code plan model that Kimi's /coding/v1/models marks supports_thinking_type "only" (K3, K3.1 Pro, K2.8) is now written with always_thinking, so Kimi Code no longer offers thinking off. Not tried against the real Kimi upstream; the e2e ran Kimi Code 2.4.1 against a fake upstream serving the real list.
